newsitem.title: UK: UK attacks China over Hong Kong civil rights curbs.
newsitem.headline: UK attacks China over Hong Kong civil rights curbs.

text.p: Britain on Thursday attacked Chinese plans to restrict civil rights in Hong Kong after the colony reverts to China on July 1, saying the move was totally unjustified.

Hong Kong's future government made some minor changes to its planned civil rights curbs on Thursday but insisted on the need to roll back recent British reforms which aimed to bring more democracy to the colony
"The (Chinese) proposals contained unnecessary restrictions and rightly aroused widespread concern both in Hong Kong and internationally," the British Foreign Office said in a statement.
"There is no justification for such amendments to the present laws."

An aide to Hong Kong leader-in-waiting Tung Cheehwa unveiled a diluted version of curbs on protests and a modified ban on foreign funding of local political groups, saying changes had been made after a three-week public consulting exercise.

But he stressed the concept of "national security" would be paramount in Hong Kong's post-handover laws, widely expected to outlaw any protests advocating independence for Taiwan or Tibet, which China regards as its rightful territory.
"It was right to consult the people of Hong Kong. We are pleased that the new proposals take some account of some of the anxieties expressed," said the Foreign Office statement.

"But we remain concerned at the elements of the revised proposals which still do not fully meet the concerns of the community and which represent a step backwards from present arrangements," it continued.

New Foreign Secretary Robin Cook vowed earlier this week that human rights would play a major role in Britain's foreign policy and said one of his priorities was a smooth handover of Hong Kong to China.
